bug_semantics: RNP 0.18.0 public-key encryption emits PKESK packets whose content-encryption key (CEK) is an all-zero byte array. init_encrypted_dst() allocates rnp::secure_bytes enckey(keylen, 0) and then calls encrypted_build_skesk() to generate the CEK and any SKESK packets. encrypted_build_skesk() returns true immediately when ctx.passwords is empty (the PKESK-only path) without calling ctx.sec_ctx.rng.get, so the zeroed buffer is encrypted to each recipient. Anyone holding the ciphertext can decrypt by supplying an all-zero session key; private keys are not required. Passphrase-based SKESK encryption still randomizes the CEK (or derives it from the password in the v4 single-password case) and is not affected.
flaw_origin: A January 2025 SKESK-writing refactor (rnpgp/rnp#2309, author Nickolay Olshevsky / ni4) moved CEK generation out of init_encrypted_dst() into a new helper encrypted_build_skesk(). Before the change, init_encrypted_dst() called ctx.sec_ctx.rng.get(enckey.data(), keylen) whenever the message was not a v4 single-password SKESK, which included every PKESK (public-recipient) encryption. The new helper only called rng.get on SKESK paths and treated empty passwords as a no-op success, dropping PKESK randomization. That first-write in the v0.18.0 ancestry is 020c61c4814d29d723b62ee4a2d2719a6b397acf (single parent, not a squash). Identical-patch public objects (patch-id fcaf7ef633abc13dc9b7c498dd0aea0819ce72f8) exist as PR member c77547b621474605550b5d1e1056ac4474253d5e and main-line 7bd9a8dc356aae756b40755be76d36205b6b161a (the SHA named by the CNA); neither is an ancestor of tag v0.18.0. Immediate parent 3574439cd2196da6397a4c9e1a7ed09390735034 still has the pre-refactor rng.get for non-singlepass, including PKESK, and has no encrypted_build_skesk().
